text.p: British-based Millennium & Copthorne Hotels Plc said on Wednesday the outlook for the group remained good in the second half of the year.
"The outlook for the group remains good - the second half has started well with July showing good growth on the same period last year," chairman Kwek Leng Beng said in a statement.
"The results of our Group tend to be weighted towards the second half of the year and I am confident we will achieve our goals for the year," added Kwek, a Singaporean entrepreneur.
Millennium & Copthorne owns and operates a range of four-star hotels in Britain, France, Germany and New York. The group was floated last year by CDL Hotels International.
It reported pre-tax profit of 19.9 million pounds ($31.4 million) in the first six months of 1997, a 53 percent increase. ($ = 0.633 British Pounds)
